content: /* ========================================================= ST. ANN'S COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY CHIRALA NON-TEACHING STAFF Standalone CSS - Header & Footer Safe ========================================================= */ .sacet-nts-wrapper { --sacet-blue: #003b73; --sacet-dark: #00264d; --sacet-yellow: #f4c400; --sacet-light-blue: #eef6ff; --sacet-light-yellow: #fff9dc; --sacet-border: #d7e2ee; --sacet-text: #1d2733; width: 100%; max-width: 1450px; margin: 30px auto; padding: 0 15px; box-sizing: border-box; font-family: "Poppins", Arial, sans-serif; color: var(--sacet-text); } /* ========================= PAGE TITLE ========================= */ .sacet-nts-title { background: linear-gradient( 135deg, var(--sacet-dark), var(--sacet-blue) ); border-radius: 14px; border-bottom: 5px solid var(--sacet-yellow); padding: 24px 20px; margin-bottom: 25px; text-align: center; box-shadow: 0 8px 25px rgba(0,0,0,0.10); } .sacet-nts-title h2 { margin: 0; padding: 0; color: #ffffff !important; font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.3; } .sacet-nts-title p { margin: 7px 0 0; padding: 0; color: #ffffff !important; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } /* ========================= SEARCH / FILTER ========================= */ .sacet-nts-controls { display: flex; gap: 15px; margin-bottom: 25px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .sacet-nts-search, .sacet-nts-filter { flex: 1; min-width: 250px; } .sacet-nts-search input, .sacet-nts-filter select { width: 100%; height: 50px; padding: 0 16px; box-sizing: border-box; border: 1px solid var(--sacet-border); border-radius: 8px; background: #ffffff; color: #222222; font-family: "Poppins", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; outline: none; transition: all 0.3s ease; } .sacet-nts-search input:focus, .sacet-nts-filter select:focus { border-color: var(--sacet-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,59,115,0.10); } /* ========================= DEPARTMENT CARD ========================= */ .sacet-nts-department { width: 100%; margin-bottom: 28px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid var(--sacet-border); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 5px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); } /* ========================= DEPARTMENT HEADER ========================= */ .sacet-nts-department-title { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 15px; padding: 14px 18px; background: var(--sacet-blue); border-left: 7px solid var(--sacet-yellow); } .sacet-nts-department-title h3 { margin: 0; padding: 0; color: #ffffff !important; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.4; } .sacet-nts-count { flex-shrink: 0; background: var(--sacet-yellow); color: #111111; padding: 5px 13px; border-radius: 30px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; } /* ========================= TABLE WRAPPER ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table-wrap { width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; } /* ========================= TABLE ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table { width: 100%; min-width: 900px; border-collapse: collapse; border-spacing: 0; margin: 0 !important; table-layout: fixed; background: #ffffff; } .sacet-nts-table thead th { background: var(--sacet-dark) !important; color: #ffffff !important; padding: 13px 10px; border: 1px solid #365879; text-align: center !important; vertical-align: middle; font-family: "Poppins", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; white-space: normal; } .sacet-nts-table tbody td { padding: 11px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--sacet-border); color: #273746; font-family: "Poppins", Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; vertical-align: middle; background: #ffffff; word-break: normal; } .sacet-nts-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) td { background: var(--sacet-light-blue); } .sacet-nts-table tbody tr:hover td { background: var(--sacet-light-yellow); } /* ========================= COLUMN WIDTHS ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(1), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(1) { width: 7%; text-align: center !important; } .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(2), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(2) { width: 9%; text-align: center !important; } .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(3), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(3) { width: 25%; } .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(4), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(4) { width: 22%; } .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(5), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(5) { width: 18%; } .sacet-nts-table th:nth-child(6), .sacet-nts-table td:nth-child(6) { width: 19%; text-align: center !important; } /* ========================= STAFF NAME ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table .staff-name { color: var(--sacet-blue) !important; font-weight: 600; } /* ========================= SERIAL NUMBER ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table .serial-no { color: var(--sacet-blue) !important; font-weight: 700; text-align: center !important; } /* ========================= JOINING DATE ========================= */ .sacet-nts-table .joining-date { text-align: center !important; white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; } /* ========================= NO RESULT ========================= */ .sacet-nts-no-result { display: none; padding: 25px; text-align: center; color: #777777; font-size: 15px; } /* ========================= NOTE ========================= */ .sacet-nts-note { margin-top: 20px; padding: 15px 18px; background: var(--sacet-light-yellow); border-left: 5px solid var(--sacet-yellow); border-radius: 7px; color: #333333; font-size: 13px; } /* ========================= MOBILE ========================= */ @media (max-width: 768px) { .sacet-nts-wrapper { margin: 20px auto; padding: 0 10px; } .sacet-nts-title { padding: 18px 12px; } .sacet-nts-title h2 { font-size: 23px; } .sacet-nts-title p { font-size: 12px; } .sacet-nts-controls { gap: 10px; } .sacet-nts-search, .sacet-nts-filter { min-width: 100%; } .sacet-nts-department-title { padding: 12px 13px; } .sacet-nts-department-title h3 { font-size: 16px; } .sacet-nts-table { min-width: 900px; } } @media (max-width: 480px) { .sacet-nts-title h2 { font-size: 20px; } .sacet-nts-department-title { flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; } .sacet-nts-table thead th, .sacet-nts-table tbody td { padding: 9px 8px; font-size: 12px; } } ``` NON-TEACHING STAFF St. Ann's College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala All Departments Administrative Office Library Department of EEE Department of ME Department of ECE Department of CSE Department of CSE-AIML Department of CSE-IOT Department of CSE-DS Department of Cyber Security Department of Civil Department of H&S Department of MBA Department of MCA Hostel Administrative Office 30 Staff S. title: Student list
content: /* Main Section */ .students-list-section { width: 100%; padding: 40px 20px; box-sizing: border-box; font-family: 'Poppins', Arial, sans-serif; } /* Heading */ .students-list-heading { text-align: center; font-size: 32px; font-weight: 700; color: #003b70; margin: 0 0 35px; position: relative; } /* Yellow underline */ .students-list-heading::after { content: ""; display: block; width: 75px; height: 4px; background: #f4c400; margin: 12px auto 0; border-radius: 10px; } /* Cards Container */ .students-list-container { max-width: 1000px; margin: 0 auto; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 25px; } /* Individual Card */ .student-list-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e2e2; border-radius: 12px; padding: 28px 20px; text-align: center; box-shadow: 0 5px 18px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08); transition: all 0.3s ease; position: relative; overflow: hidden; } /* Top Yellow Line */ .student-list-card::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 4px; background: #f4c400; } /* Hover */ .student-list-card:hover { transform: translateY(-6px); box-shadow: 0 12px 28px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14); border-color: #003b70; } /* Year Title */ .student-list-title { font-size: 23px; font-weight: 700; color: #003b70; margin: 8px 0 18px; } /* View Button */ .student-view-btn { display: inline-block; padding: 10px 30px; background: #f4c400; color: #111111 !important; text-decoration: none !important; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; transition: all 0.3s ease; } /* Button Hover */ .student-view-btn:hover { background: #003b70; color: #ffffff !important; transform: scale(1.05); } /* Tablet */ @media (max-width: 900px) { .students-list-container { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); } } /* Mobile */ @media (max-width: 600px) { .students-list-section { padding: 30px 15px; } .students-list-heading { font-size: 26px; } .students-list-container { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 18px; } .student-list-card { padding: 25px 20px; } } Students List 2-1 View 3-1 View 4-1 View

title: R26 Regulation
content: R26 CURRICULUM R26 Program Structure & Syllabus Explore the R26 Program Structure and Syllabus for Undergraduate Engineering programmes offered by St. Ann's College of Engineering & Technology. 01 CS CSE – Cyber Security Computer Science & Engineering with specialization in Cyber Security. View R26 Syllabus → 02 CSE CSE Computer Science & Engineering R26 Program Structure and Syllabus. View R26 Syllabus → 03 ECE ECE Electronics & Communication Engineering R26 Program Structure and Syllabus. View R26 Syllabus → 04 IoT CSE – IoT Computer Science & Engineering with specialization in Internet of Things. View R26 Syllabus → 05 DS CSE – Data Science Computer Science & Engineering with specialization in Data Science. View R26 Syllabus → 06 AI CSE – AI & ML Computer Science & Engineering with specialization in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning. View R26 Syllabus → 07 ME Mechanical Engineering Mechanical Engineering R26 Program Structure and Syllabus. View R26 Syllabus → 08 EEE EEE Electrical & Electronics Engineering R26 Program Structure and Syllabus. View R26 Syllabus → 09 CE Civil Engineering Civil Engineering R26 Program Structure and Syllabus. View R26 Syllabus → /* ========================================================= SACET R26 PROGRAM STRUCTURE & SYLLABUS ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 75px 20px 90px; background: radial-gradient( circle at 5% 10%, rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.12), transparent 27% ), radial-gradient( circle at 95% 90%, rgba(0, 82, 155, 0.10), transparent 30% ), #f5f8fc; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; color: #172033; position: relative; overflow: hidden; } /* ========================================================= DECORATIVE ELEMENTS ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus::before { content: ""; position: absolute; width: 360px; height: 360px; border-radius: 50%; top: -210px; left: -170px; border: 50px solid rgba(0, 82, 155, 0.045); pointer-events: none; } #sacet-r26-syllabus::after { content: ""; position: absolute; width: 300px; height: 300px; border-radius: 50%; right: -150px; bottom: -150px; border: 45px solid rgba(255, 193, 7, 0.07); pointer-events: none; } /* ========================================================= CONTAINER ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-container { width: 100%; max-width: 1450px; margin: 0 auto; position: relative; z-index: 2; } /* ========================================================= HEADER ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-header { max-width: 850px; margin: 0 auto 52px; text-align: center; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 8px 18px; border-radius: 50px; background: #00529b; color: #ffffff; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.5px; margin-bottom: 15px; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-header h2 { margin: 0 0 15px; font-size: clamp(30px, 4vw, 48px); line-height: 1.15; font-weight: 800; color: #0b2442; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-header h2 span { color: #00529b; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-header p { margin: 0 auto; max-width: 780px; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #667085; } /* ========================================================= PROGRAM GRID ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 25px; } /* ========================================================= CARD ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card { position: relative; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e3eaf2; border-radius: 18px; padding: 32px 28px 29px; min-height: 310px; box-sizing: border-box; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(20, 45, 75, 0.07); transition: transform 0.35s ease, box-shadow 0.35s ease, border-color 0.35s ease; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card:hover { transform: translateY(-8px); border-color: #00529b; box-shadow: 0 20px 45px rgba(20, 45, 75, 0.14); } /* TOP LINE */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 100%; height: 5px; background: linear-gradient( 90deg, #00529b, #ffc107 ); } /* ========================================================= CARD NUMBER ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-number { position: absolute; right: 20px; top: 17px; font-size: 44px; line-height: 1; font-weight: 900; color: rgba(0, 82, 155, 0.055); user-select: none; } /* ========================================================= ICON ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-icon { width: 68px; height: 68px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 16px; background: linear-gradient( 135deg, #00529b, #0074c8 ); color: #ffffff; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.5px; margin-bottom: 22px; box-shadow: 0 10px 22px rgba(0, 82, 155, 0.20); transition: transform 0.3s ease; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card:hover .r26-icon { transform: rotate(-4deg) scale(1.06); } /* ========================================================= CARD CONTENT ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card-content h3 { margin: 0 0 11px; font-size: 20px; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 750; color: #102a43; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-card-content p { margin: 0 0 22px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.7; color: #667085; min-height: 72px; } /* ========================================================= BUTTON ========================================================= */ #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-button { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; padding: 11px 18px; border-radius: 8px; background: #00529b; color: #ffffff !important; text-decoration: none !important; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; transition: background 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease; } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-button:hover { background: #003f78; transform: translateY(-2px); } #sacet-r26-syllabus .r26-button span { font-size: 18px; Details of admission policy, statistics, fee structure and student support for academic year 2025–2026. S.No. Item Details to be Provided 6.1 Admission Policy and Process Criteria: As per the Andhra Pradesh State Government admission policy. Reservation policy: As per AP State Government rules. Entrance exams: AP EAPCET — for B.Tech AP ICET — for MCA and MBA APPGECET and GATE — for M.Tech Detailed admission brochure and process links are available on the college website/admissions portal. 6.2 Year-wise Admission Statistics Academic Year: 2025–2026 Intake: B.Tech — 960; M.Tech — 144; MBA — 120; MCA — 60. Applications / Admissions: 70% seats filled via State Govt counselling; Admitted: B.Tech — 977 (including 10% EWS quota), M.Tech — 115, MBA — 132 (including 10% EWS quota), MCA — 53. Complete admission statistics (category-wise, gender-wise, region-wise) are available in annexure or institutional MIS. 6.3 Fee Structure Course-wise: Fees fixed as per AFRC. Typical fees: B.Tech — Rs. 56,800/-; MBA & MCA — Rs. 35,000/-; M.Tech — Rs. 50,000/- (as notified). Refund policy: Full refund of fee (minus processing fee up to Rs. 1,000) if a student withdraws before course commencement. If withdrawal happens after course start and the seat is filled, refund is pro-rated for the period occupied (minus deductions). ANNEXURE – 6_3 Attach official fee notification, AFRC order and refund rules (annexure). 6.4 Scholarships and Financial Aid Institutional/Government/Endowment support: Provided as per State Government policy and institute-specific endowments. Details of scholarship schemes, eligibility and application process can be found on the scholarships page or in annexures. 6.5 Student Demographics Gender, category and region distribution, nationality: Maintained as per State Government reservation rules and institutional records. Downloadable demographic breakdown available from institutional MIS (category-wise, gender-wise, region-wise). 6.6 Mentoring and Counseling Academic & Personal Mentoring: Mentor-to-student ratio — 1 mentor per 20 students. Details about mentoring assignments, counselling hours, and mental health resources are available with Student Affairs or Counselling Cell. 6.7 Student Grievance Redressal Link to Grievance Redressal Committee is available under Non-Statutory Committees on the website. Online grievance filing mechanism and committee contact details provided on the institutional portal. 6.8 Anti-Ragging Measures Link to Anti-Ragging Committee available under Non-Statutory Committees on the website; ragging prevention measures and helpline numbers are displayed across campus. Anti-ragging affidavits and monitoring committee details are maintained as per UGC/AICTE rules. 6.9 Alumni Network Link to Alumni Committee available under Non-Statutory Committees; alumni engagement, placement support and mentoring initiatives are coordinated via Alumni Office.

title: M.Tech
content: M.Tech Programs at St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology At St. Ann’s College of Engineering and Technology, we offer a range of advanced postgraduate programs designed to empower the next generation of engineers and technologists. Our M.Tech courses provide in-depth knowledge, hands-on experience, and research opportunities in cutting-edge fields, tailored to meet industry demands and technological advancements. Specializations Offered Embedded Systems (Year of Start – 2013) Dive into the world of microcontrollers, IoT devices, real-time systems, and hardware-software integration. Our Embedded Systems specialization equips students with the skills needed to design and develop intelligent embedded solutions for various industries. Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI & ML) (Year of Start – 2025) Explore advanced concepts in AI, deep learning, data mining, and predictive analytics. This specialization prepares students to innovate and solve complex problems using intelligent algorithms and data-driven techniques. Computer Science and Engineering (Year of Start – 2007) Gain expertise in software development, data structures, algorithms, and emerging technologies such as cloud computing, cybersecurity, and big data. This program fosters strong problem-solving and research skills in core computer science. Power Systems (Year of Start – 2013) Focus on the analysis, design, and management of electrical power generation, transmission, and distribution systems. This specialization prepares students for challenges in renewable energy, smart grids, and sustainable power solutions. Transportation Engineering (Year of start – 2015) Learn the principles of planning, design, operation, and maintenance of transportation systems. This program emphasizes sustainable and efficient transport infrastructure development. Thermal Engineering (Year of Start – 2014) Study the fundamentals and applications of thermodynamics, heat transfer, and energy systems. This specialization is ideal for those aiming to excel in energy management, HVAC systems, and thermal power plants. Intake Capacity Each specialization admits 24 students per academic year, ensuring a focused and interactive learning environment.

} } Internal Complaints Committee Preamble Roles & Responsibilities ICC Committee Members POSH Act Preamble of the Internal Complaints Committee The Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) is established to promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment within our institution. Recognizing the right of every individual to work and study in an atmosphere free from harassment and discrimination, the ICC is committed to addressing grievances related to sexual harassment and any form of misconduct. The committee aims to create awareness about the issues of harassment and to provide a platform for individuals to voice their concerns without fear of retaliation. Through transparent procedures and fair investigations, the ICC will ensure that complaints are handled promptly and sensitively. We believe that fostering a culture of respect, dignity, and equality is paramount to the well-being of our community. The ICC is dedicated to implementing preventive measures, conducting educational programs, and promoting a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of harassment. By encouraging open dialogue and supporting affected individuals, we strive to maintain a safe and supportive environment for all. Roles, Responsibilities and Statutes SACET is a coeducational institution providing equal opportunities to all and is working towards providing a congenial atmosphere for men and women to work together. SACET has formed an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), as mandated by the regulatory authorities and POSH Act, to address and initiate appropriate action on complaints involving physical contacts or advances, demand for sexual favours, sexually tainted remarks, and any unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal expressions of a sexual nature. Any aggrieved person (employee, visitor or student) who has suffered harassment at the workplace can approach the ICC. This committee aims at sensitizing the students and staff to work diligently to prevent sexual harassment in the college and work towards the redressal of sexual harassment cases. The functions of ICC shall be to: Prevent sexual harassment at the workplace. Prevent discrimination and sexual harassment against girls by promoting gender amity among students and employees. Conduct periodical programmes on women empowerment. Provide a conducive environment and congenial atmosphere for women. content: A Six Day FDP on POWER CONVERTERS AND CONTROL TECHNIQUES FOR MICROGRIDS AND ELECTRIC VEHICLES Proposed Title & Objective About The Institute About the Department Topics Covered Under FDP Proposed Title: Power Converters and Control Techniques for Microgrids and Electric vehicles Objective: The proposed FDP on “ Power Converters and Control Techniques for Microgrids and Electric vehicles ”isaspecializedprogramthatfocuses on state of art technologies related to converter design and control for microgrid and electrical vehicles. This FDPtargets the research scholars working in the respective domains, to clarify their doubts in their relevant working research topics. This also helps the faculty to update their knowledge in the respective domains to give better understanding in the topics in the newly introduced courses. It helps the students to meet the current industry requirement. It also supports start-up entrepreneurs in the respective areas. St. Ann's College of Engineering & Technology (SACET) was established in the year2001 at Vetapalem Mandal, Chirala, Prakasam District, Andhra Pradesh bythe St. MaryEducational Society, pioneered by Educationalists, Industrialists and Philanthropists. TheCollege is housed amidst lush green fields, in serene environment, free from pollution andconductiveforthepursuitofeducation. TheInstitutionisApprovedbyAICTE,NewDelhiandseveral departments of the Institute are Accredited by National Board of Accreditation(NBA) multiple times and also the Institution has permanent membership in Institution ofEngineers(I).TheinstituteisAutonomous fromtheacademicyear2023-24onwards. The Institution is Accredited by NAAC with ‘A’ Grade in I, II and III cycles .Recognized by UGC Under Section 2(f) and 12(B) of UGC Act, 1956 and also Awarded ‘A’GradebyAndhraPradeshStateGovernment.ThecollegehasMOUwithISROSpaceApplication Center, Ahmadabad and received 3 IRNSS receiver kits for GPS data collection.The college is approved as TSDI [SEIMENS] by AP State Government. The institution hasorganizedvarious governmentfunded andInstitutionfundedFDPsandWorkshops. About the Department: From a modest beginning in 2001, the Electrical and Electronics Engineering Department in St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology (SACET), Chirala has now grown into a fully integrated department in the field of Engineering and Technology. It is an “education with future”. Learning how to inquire, converse and collaborate, the skill that never go out of date. The objectives of imparting education, combined with creation, dissemination and application of knowledge are being met in an integrated form to create a synergetic impact. To fulfill its mission in new and powerful ways, faculty, staff and student of the department strives to achieve excellence in every endeavour – be it education, research, consulting or training-by making continuous improvements in curricula and pedagogical tools. The faculty of the department published research papers in various reputed international journals and conferences with good number of papers published in SCOPUS/SCI indexed journals. The department of EEE has surpassed many milestones under the able and dynamic leadership of its HOD Dr. SVD Anil Kumar. Some of the notable achievements are: UG NBA accreditation – 2009-2016 NAAC Accreditation 2011 and 2016 Controller of Examinations – 2006 to till date Overview of power converters for renewable energy systems. Mathematical Modelling and Simulation of Microgrid FPGA implementation in Power electronic converters DG penetration and Power Quality assessment and mitigation in Distribution Network Design switched-mode power converters for RE and EV systems. Impact of EV charging station on distribution system Electric Vehicle chargers design and optimization techniques Real time and Virtual simulations on EV, BMS and Microgrid Applications V2G &G2V systems & issues. Reliability Aspects of Power Electronics Converters Model based development for EV applications in MATLAB Coordinator The Co-ordinatorpublished more than 35 Research papers in international journals and conferences. His research interests are mainly focused on Harmonic analysis in power systems. He also has rich experience in organizing various funded FDPs and workshops. title: ALL ABOUT CIVIL
content: NAAC NAAC AQAR SYLLABUS RESULTS IQAC MINUTES JOBS & CARRIERS DEPARTMENTS PLACEMENTS EXAMINATIONS CELLS IQAC COMMITTEES NOTIFICATIONS FACILITIES FACULTY RESEARCH COLLAGE TOUR ALL ABOUT CIVIL The department of Civil Engineering was established in the year 2011 with an intake of 60. Eight batches of students nearly 480 have successfully completed their graduation so far from the department. Our strength is our faculty. We have twelve dedicated faculty members and three supporting staff members. In 2015 the department has also started Master of Technology (M. Tech) programme with initial intake of 24 students with Transportation Engineering as specialization. The department has nine physical laboratories to fulfill the needs of academic and industrial requirements including are Concrete, Transportation Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering , Environmental Engineering , Survey , Geology , Hydraulic Engineering , Computer aided engineering , GIS & CAD lab, Strength of materials, FM & HM Lab and Irrigation Design and Drawing. All laboratories are equipped with state of the art equipment to suit the emerging technologies and career opportunities The students are prepared with multi-dimensional skill sets covering all the required graduate attributes. More focus is given on practical learning, projects, and research. The department is plans guest lecturers from industry personnel, industrial visits and tours every year to fill the gap between academia and industry. The department is also conducting workshops and conferences at regular intervals in the latest and innovative areas of civil engineering. The board of studies of civil engineering is constituted by taking the services emerging technologies career of students. Many students are qualified in Gate Exam, got placements in civil engineering core companies, Sachivalayam jobs as well. With software career options open for aspiring civil engineering students so far 50 students were placed in companies like Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Capgemini, Amazon, Virtusa, Sutherland etc. VISION To become a nationally recognized centre for Civil Engineering Education with effective Teaching and Learning practices MISSION DM1: To produce competent Civil Engineering students with ability to design, develop and problem solving skills. DM2: To produce students with ability to use modern tools along with life long learning skills.. DM3: To promote entrepreneurship and soft skills. DM4: To promote industry interaction, consultancy and concern for the society.

title: About our College
content: ALL ABOUT THE COLLEGE St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology – AUTONOMOUS (Non-Minority College) was established in the year 2001 at Vetapalem Mandal, Chirala, Bapatla District, Andhra Pradesh by The St. Mary Educational Society, pioneered by Educationalists, Industrialists and Philanthropists. The College is housed amidst lush green fields, in serene environment, free from pollution and conductive for the pursuit of education. Bay of Bengal is just two km away from the college. The Institution is Approved by All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi and is Permanently Affiliated to the Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada.Five Programmes were Accredited by National Board of Accredition(NBA).The Institution is Accredited by NAAC with ‘A’ Grade.The Institution is recognized by UGC under section 2(f) and 12(B).The Institution is awarded ‘A’ grade by Andhra Pradesh State Government. The Institution is Permanently Accredited by Institution of Engineers(I).Institution is selected for Andhra Pradesh State Technical Skill Development Center(Siemens).The College has a glory of experience in teaching from 2001 onwards. The College is situated along the Bypass Road at 6 KMs distance Chirala town in Chirala-Ongole stretch. The College campus has a sprawling area of around 24.3 1/2 acres, with serene atmosphere, sylvan settings and environs, conductive for academic activities. The college is well connected by rail and road links because of its ideal location. VISION To develop St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology – AUTONOMOUS into an Institution of Global standards catering to the educational needs of students and also contribute to the welfare of local Community. MISSION To impart total quality education at Under Graduate and Post Graduate levels by: Inculcating best teaching and learning practices; providing opportunities for faculty development, Consultancy, Research; striving for maximum results in the examinations; Creating avenues for industry interaction to provide training and placement opportunities; managing the institution with good governance and transparency and strive for well-being of local community.

title: ABOUT AIML
content: ALL ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT AI and Machine Learning jobs have jumped by almost 75 percent over the past four years and are poised to keep growing. Similar to data analysts, statisticians, and business analysts, AI is one of the fastest growing, in-demand fields and lucrative career choices. A study by Oxford University and Yale University indicates that AI will outperform humans in many ways and will automate all human jobs in the next 120 years. By 2024, AI will be better than humans at translation, will write bestselling books by 2049, and will perform surgeries by 2053. The global conversational AI market size was valued at USD 5.78 billion in 2020 and is projected to reach USD 32.62 billion by 2030, registering a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 20.0% from 2021 to 2030. The field of artificial intelligence has a tremendous career outlook, with the Bureau of Labor Statistics predicting a 31.4 percent, by 2030, increase in jobs for data scientists and mathematical science professionals, which are crucial to AI. In their global AI study, PwC estimates that by 2030, the global GDP will have increased by 26 percent due to AI alone. That’s more than the current GDP of China and India combined. PwC isn’t the only optimist in the room. The World Economic Forum estimates that 97 million new jobs will be created through AI by 2025. With a humongous amount of data becoming more available today, Machine Learning is starting to move to the cloud. Data Scientists will no longer explicitly custom code or manage infrastructure. A.I. and ML will help the systems to scale for them, generate new models on the go and deliver faster and accurate results. Pursuing a machine learning job is a solid choice for a high-paying career that will be in demand for decades. AIML provides applications that have an ability to learn through the experience without being explicitly programmed. Machine Learniing enables applications to recognize patterns in the data in the same way as human brains do. It has become an integral part of our day to day lives and few of the widely used applications are Traffic Alerts, Social Media (Facebook, Twitter), Product Recommendations (Amazon, FlipKart), Virtual Personal Assistants (Siri, Google Assist), Directions in Google maps, Self-Driving Cars, Online Video Streaming (NetFlix). As per the recent reports, AI/ ML Engineer is the best job of 2021 due to the growing skill demand that attracts high salaries. AI/ ML professionals are getting an annual hike of 20-30% when compared to other skill areas. Starting such a program is a step towards fulfilling the high skill demand for AI/ ML professionals across the globe. AIML Started in 2021 with an Intake of 60 Intake Increased to 120 in 2025-26

KNOW MORE ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT The department of CSE-Data Science was established in the year 2021 with an intake of 60 with AICTE approval. The department has well equipped computer laboratories, and full-fledged faculty members. Data science is the study of large amount data to extract meaningful insights for decision making in the different area of life such as business, education and research, diagnostics etc. It is a multidisciplinary approach that combines principles and practices from the fields of mathematics, statistics, artificial intelligence, and computer engineering to analyze large amounts of data. This analysis helps data scientists to ask and answer questions like what happened, why it happened, what will happen, and what can be done with the results. KNOW MORE VISION The Department of Data Science trains the next generation of students as data scientists who will modelreal world challenges andinnovate solutions through world-class research to take advantage of large amount data availability. title: Internet of Things(IoT)
content: CSE – Internet of Things Connecting The Intelligent World. Explore the future of connected intelligence where sensors, embedded systems, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and smart technologies come together to transform the physical world into an intelligent ecosystem. Explore IoT Discover Our Programme 01 Connected Systems 02 Smart Technologies 03 Future Ready Skills S C A C D N IoT SMART DEVICES CONNECTED INTELLIGENCE Sensors   •   Embedded Systems   •   Cloud Computing   •   Artificial Intelligence   •   Smart Automation @keyframes rotateRing { from { transform:rotate(0deg); } to { transform:rotate(360deg); } } @media (max-width:900px) { .iot-mobile-placeholder { display:none; } } About the Department About HOD Faculty VIsion & Mission PEOs, PSOs, POs Student Conferance Publications Student Publications - Journals Workshops & Guest Lectures Faculty Research & Publications News Letters/Magazine BOS About the Department @keyframes iotMove { 0%{transform:translate(0,0);opacity:.35} 50%{transform:translate(35px,-25px);opacity:.8} 100%{transform:translate(0,0);opacity:.35} } @keyframes iotPulse { 0%,100%{transform:scale(1);opacity:.4} 50%{transform:scale(1.8);opacity:1} } @keyframes iotLine { 0%{opacity:.1} 50%{opacity:.6} 100%{opacity:.1} } @keyframes iotFloat { 0%{transform:translateY(0)} 50%{transform:translateY(-25px)} 100%{transform:translateY(0)} } Internet of Things (IoT) Connecting the Physical World with Digital Intelligence Introduction to IoT The Internet of Things (IoT) refers to the rapidly growing network of physical devices, machines, vehicles, appliances, sensors and other objects that are connected to the Internet and capable of collecting, processing and exchanging data. These connected devices use sensors, software, communication technologies and computing systems to gather information from their surroundings. The collected information can then be transmitted through wired or wireless networks to other devices, applications or cloud platforms for processing and analysis. With the availability of low-cost computer chips, sensors, cloud computing and high-speed wireless networks, almost any physical object can become part of an IoT ecosystem. From smart watches and home appliances to industrial machines, automobiles, agricultural equipment and aircraft, IoT is creating a connected environment where physical objects can communicate and exchange information with minimal human intervention. What Makes IoT Different? Traditional devices generally perform a specific function without being able to understand or communicate information about their surroundings. IoT adds a layer of digital intelligence by connecting these devices to networks and equipping them with sensors and software. For example, a traditional temperature sensor may simply display the temperature. An IoT-enabled temperature sensor can continuously measure the temperature, send the information to a cloud platform, analyze the data and automatically trigger an action when a particular threshold is reached. Key Components of IoT Sensors & Devices Sensors collect information from the physical environment such as temperature, humidity, pressure, motion, location, light, sound and vibration. Connectivity IoT devices communicate using technologies such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular networks, Zigbee, RFID, LoRaWAN and other communication protocols. Data Processing Collected data is processed using edge computing, cloud platforms and specialized software to identify patterns and generate useful information. Applications & Users Applications transform processed data into meaningful insights, dashboards, alerts, recommendations and automated actions. How Does IoT Work? An IoT system generally follows a continuous cycle of sensing, communication, processing, analysis and action. The process can be summarized as follows: 01 Sense Sensors collect information from the environment. 02 Connect The device transmits data through a network. 03 Process Data is processed locally or in the cloud. 04 Analyze Software analyzes the collected information. 05 Act The system generates an alert or performs an action. Applications of IoT Smart Homes IoT enables smart lighting, smart thermostats, security cameras, door locks, appliances and energy management systems that can be monitored and controlled remotely. Healthcare Connected medical devices and wearable technologies can collect and transmit health-related measurements, support remote monitoring and help healthcare professionals make informed decisions. Smart Agriculture IoT sensors can monitor soil moisture, temperature, weather conditions and crop environments, helping farmers improve irrigation, resource utilization and agricultural productivity. Industrial IoT Factories use connected machines and sensors to monitor equipment performance, detect abnormalities, optimize production and support predictive maintenance. Smart Cities IoT technologies can support intelligent traffic management, smart parking, waste management, public lighting, environmental monitoring and energy management. Connected Vehicles Modern vehicles can use IoT technologies for location tracking, vehicle diagnostics, navigation, safety systems, fleet management and communication with other systems. Benefits of IoT Automation: IoT systems can automate repetitive tasks and processes. Real-Time Monitoring: Devices can provide continuous information about equipment, environments and operations. Improved Efficiency: Data-driven systems can help organizations use energy, materials, time and other resources more efficiently. Predictive Maintenance: Sensors can identify unusual patterns and potential equipment failures before they become serious problems. Better Decision Making: Real-time data and analytics can support faster and more informed decisions. Enhanced User Experience: Connected products can provide personalized, responsive and convenient services. IoT, Big Data and Artificial Intelligence IoT devices can generate enormous amounts of data because they continuously collect information from the physical world. This data becomes especially valuable when combined with Big Data analytics and Artificial Intelligence (AI) . AI and machine learning algorithms can analyze IoT data to identify patterns, predict future events and support automated decision-making. This combination is helping organizations move from simple monitoring systems toward intelligent and autonomous systems. Challenges of IoT Security Large numbers of connected devices increase the potential attack surface and require strong security measures. Privacy Connected devices may collect sensitive or personal information, making responsible data management important. Interoperability Different manufacturers and platforms may use different technologies and communication standards. Data Management The enormous volume of information generated by IoT devices requires scalable storage, processing and analytics infrastructure. Future of IoT The future of IoT is closely connected with developments in artificial intelligence, edge computing, advanced sensors, cloud computing, robotics and next-generation wireless networks. As these technologies continue to evolve, IoT systems are expected to become more intelligent, efficient and autonomous. The integration of IoT with AI and machine learning will enable systems to understand their environments, predict events and take appropriate actions with limited human intervention. This can create new opportunities across healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, agriculture, education, energy and smart-city development. Conclusion The Internet of Things is transforming ordinary physical objects into connected and intelligent systems. By combining sensors, connectivity, computing and data analytics, IoT enables devices to collect information, communicate with one another and respond to changing conditions. From smart homes and healthcare to agriculture, manufacturing and smart cities, IoT is becoming an important part of modern digital transformation. As connectivity and intelligent technologies continue to advance, IoT will play an increasingly important role in creating a more connected, efficient and responsive world. PEO1 Engineering Knowledge & IoT Solutions Graduates apply knowledge of computing, electronics, embedded systems and IoT to design effective engineering solutions. PEO2 Professional Careers Graduates build successful careers in IoT, computing and related engineering domains. PEO3 Higher Education, Research & Innovation Graduates pursue higher education, research, innovation or entrepreneurship with a commitment to lifelong learning. PEO4 Professionalism, Ethics & Sustainable Solutions Graduates demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, ethics, collaboration with industry and research bodies to develop sustainable IoT-based solutions for societal needs. Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs) CSE–IoT graduates will be able to: PSO1 IoT Design, Development & Deployment Acquire knowledge on the design, development and deployment of CSE and IoT based solutions using sensors, microcontrollers, embedded systems, network protocols, cloud services and analytics tools. PSO2 Industry-Oriented Projects Apply cutting-edge techniques and tools to develop CSE-IoT based projects individually or in teamwork to address industrial challenges. PSO3 IoT Data Analytics & Security Analyse IoT data using machine learning techniques and apply security principles to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and resilience of IoT systems. PO1 Engineering Knowledge Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems. (WK1 to WK4) WK1 – WK4 PO3 Design/Development of Solutions Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/ processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5) WK5 PO4 Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8). (WK2 and WK6) WK2 & WK6 PO6 The Engineer and The World Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7). WK1, WK5 & WK7 PO7 Ethics Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT The Internet of Things, or IoT, refers to the billions of physical devices around the world that are now connected to the internet, all collecting and sharing data. Thanks to the arrival of super-cheap computer chips and the ubiquity of wireless networks, it’s possible to turn anything, from something as small as a pill to something as big as an aeroplane , into a part of the IoT. Connecting up all these different objects and adding sensors to them adds a level of digital intelligence to devices that would be otherwise dumb, enabling them to communicate real-time data without involving a human being. The Internet of Things is making the fabric of the world around us more smarter and more responsive, merging the digital and physical universes. JOIN US ABOUT HEAD OF THE DEPARTMENT Dr Indraneel is a Ratified Professor from JNTUK and guiding 4 Ph.D Scholars from ANNAMALAI UNIVERSITY, Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu as external supervisor. He is a peer reviewer and editorial board member for various journals like Elsevier, i-manager’s JCOM journalas etc. He got appreciation from APSSSDC for best services as SPOC-APPSSDC-SIEMENS-TSDI Centre in SACET in 2017 KNOW MORE VISION To develop the CSE–IoT department into a centre of excellence in computing and Internet of Things by imparting quality education, fostering innovation and providing industry-aligned skills that empower students to contribute to technological advancement and the welfare of society. MISSION The CSE–IoT department strives: M1: To provide strong foundations in computing, IoT technologies and interdisciplinary problem solving through effective teaching–learning practices. M2: To promote research, innovation and continuous professional development of faculty and students. M3: To enhance employability through industry collaborations, internships, training and placement support in emerging IoT and related domains. M4: To inculcate ethical values, social responsibility and commitment to community welfare through technology-enabled solutions. M5: To ensure transparent and student-centric academic processes aligned with global standards in engineering education. Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) Program Outcomes (POs) Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs) BOS PEO1: Graduates apply knowledge of computing, electronics, embedded systems and IoT to design effective engineering solutions. PEO2: Graduates build successful careers in IoT, computing and related engineering domains. PEO3: Graduates pursue higher education, research, innovation or entrepreneurship with a commitment to lifelong learning. PEO4: Graduates demonstrate professionalism, teamwork, ethics, collaboration with industry and research bodies to develop sustainable IoT-based solutions for societal needs. PO1: Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems. PO2: Problem analysis: Identity, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences. PO3: Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. PO4: Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions. PO5: Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations. PO6: The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice. PO7: Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development. PO8: Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice. PO9: Individual and teamwork: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings. PO10: Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions. PO11: Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one's work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments. PO12: Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change. CSE–IoT graduates will be able to: PSO1: Acquire knowledge on the Design, development and deployment of CSE and IoT based solutions using sensors, microcontrollers, embedded systems, network protocols, cloud services and analytics tools. PSO2: Apply cutting-edge techniques and tools to develop CSE-IoT based projects individually or in a team work to address industrial challenges. PSO3: Analyse IoT data using machine learning techniques and apply security principles to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and resilience of IoT systems. content: Department of CSE Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning Empowering students with advanced knowledge in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Data Analytics and intelligent computing technologies to solve real-world challenges. Explore Department → View Programs 🧠 AI + ML Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Deep Learning Data Analytics ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT Shaping the Future with Artificial Intelligence The Department of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning focuses on quality education, innovative research, industry interaction and the development of intelligent solutions for real-world applications. About the Department About HOD Faculty VIsion & Mission PEOs, PSOs, POs Student Conferance Publications Student Publications - Journals Faculty Publications - Journals Workshops & Guest Lectures Faculty Research & Publications Magazine News Letters Patents About the Department Career Outlook Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning A Fast-Growing Career Domain Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as some of the most transformative technologies of the 21st century. Organizations across industries are increasingly adopting intelligent systems to automate processes, analyze large volumes of data, improve decision-making, personalize customer experiences, and develop innovative products and services. As a result, demand for professionals with expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and related technologies continues to increase. For students with strong foundations in mathematics, programming, statistics, and problem-solving, AI & ML offers a wide range of exciting and rewarding career opportunities. 75% Growth in AI & Machine Learning jobs over the referenced four-year period HIGH DEMAND AI is among the fastest-growing technology and career domains GLOBAL AI skills are relevant across industries and geographical markets Why Choose AI & Machine Learning? Industry Demand AI expertise is increasingly required in technology, finance, healthcare, manufacturing, education, retail, transportation, cybersecurity, and many other sectors. Lucrative Careers Professionals with specialized AI and ML skills can pursue technically challenging and financially rewarding careers. Innovation AI enables the development of intelligent products, automated systems, predictive models, recommendation engines, and advanced digital solutions. Career Opportunities in AI & ML AI Engineer Designs and develops intelligent software systems and AI-powered applications. Machine Learning Engineer Builds, trains, evaluates, and deploys machine learning models. Data Scientist Extracts insights from complex datasets using statistics, programming, and machine learning. Deep Learning Engineer Develops neural-network-based solutions for complex AI applications. NLP Engineer Develops systems capable of understanding and processing human language. Computer Vision Engineer Creates AI systems that interpret and analyze images, video, and visual information. AI Researcher Conducts research to develop new algorithms, models, and intelligent computing techniques. AI Product Specialist Combines technology and business knowledge to develop AI-enabled products and services. The Future of Artificial Intelligence Research into the future impact of Artificial Intelligence has highlighted the possibility that increasingly capable AI systems could outperform humans in a growing number of specialized tasks. Forecasts have suggested that AI could significantly transform areas such as translation, content creation, scientific research, healthcare, and surgery. Earlier forecasts associated with research from Oxford and Yale University proposed specific milestones for AI capabilities, including advances in translation, writing, and surgical procedures. Such forecasts should be viewed as projections rather than guaranteed dates, because the pace and direction of AI development depend on technological, economic, regulatory, and societal factors. Future Outlook AI is expected to continue reshaping the nature of work rather than simply eliminating every job. Many occupations are likely to change as AI automates routine activities while increasing the value of human capabilities such as creativity, critical thinking, leadership, communication, domain expertise, and ethical judgment. Students who develop strong technical foundations and continuously update their AI skills can position themselves well for this evolving employment landscape. About HOD Dr. Hari Kishan Chapala Dr. Hari Kishan Chapala has received Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering in 2013 from Acharya Nagarjuna University, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. He is working as Professor and Head in the Department of CSE – AI & ML , St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology, Chirala. He has a total of 26 years of experience in Teaching and Administration. He is ratified by JNTUK, Kakinada in 2016. He has authored and published more than 25 research papers in reputed journals and presented papers in 8 International Conferences. He has 12 patent publications and has secured four Best Teacher Awards in recognition of his contribution to teaching and education. He is nominated as Q-Leader by APSCHE. box-shadow: none; } } VIsion & Mission 👁 VISION To build the Department of Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning into a Centre of Excellence that nurtures globally competent professionals, advances innovative research, and delivers AI-driven solutions for societal and local community development. MISSION 1 To impart quality education in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning through innovative teaching-learning processes and a curriculum aligned with global standards. 2 To promote continuous faculty development, interdisciplinary research, consultancy, and industry-institute interaction in emerging areas of Artificial Intelligence. 3 To equip students with strong analytical, programming, and problem-solving skills through experiential learning, enabling academic excellence and professional competence. 4 To inculcate ethical values, social responsibility, and the application of Artificial Intelligence technologies for sustainable development and societal welfare. PEOs, PSOs, POs PEOs PSOs POs WKs Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) PEO 1 To empower graduates to apply fundamental engineering concepts and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning principles to analyze, design, and implement effective solutions for complex real-world problems. PEO 2 To prepare graduates with advanced technical skills and professional competence to excel in careers and innovative projects in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. PEO 3 To nurture graduates with an entrepreneurial mindset, ethical awareness, teamwork and communication skills, and lifelong learning abilities to contribute effectively to society and national economic development. Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs) PSO 1 Apply core principles of computer science and engineering to design, develop, and evaluate intelligent computing systems using Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Data Analytics for real-world applications. PSO 2 Analyze and process structured and unstructured data to build, optimize, and deploy end-to-end AI&ML solutions using modern tools, frameworks, cloud platforms, and engineering practices. PSO 3 Apply ethical, transparent, secure, and socially responsible practices in the development, deployment, and use of AI and ML technologies. Program Outcomes (POs) Graduates of the programme are expected to attain the following Program Outcomes. PO1: Engineering Knowledge Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems. WK1 – WK4 PO2: Problem Analysis Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4) WK1 – WK4 PO3: Design/Development of Solutions Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/ processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5) WK5 PO4: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8). WK8 PO5: Engineering Tool Usage Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6) WK2 & WK6 PO6: The Engineer and The World Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7). WK1, WK5 & WK7 PO7: Ethics Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9) WK9 PO8: Individual and Collaborative Team Work Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams. TEAM WORK PO9: Communication Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences. COMMUNICATION PO10: Project Management and Finance Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments. MANAGEMENT & FINANCE PO11: Life-Long Learning Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8) WK8 Knowledge and Attitude Profile Knowledge and Attitude Profile – WK1 to WK9 WK1 Natural Sciences & Social Sciences Systematic, theory-based understanding of natural sciences applicable to the discipline, with awareness of relevant social sciences. WK2 Mathematics, Data Analysis & Computing Conceptually based mathematics, numerical analysis, data analysis, statistics, and formal aspects of computer/information science supporting analysis and modelling. WK3 Engineering Fundamentals Systematic, theory-based formulation of engineering fundamentals required in the engineering discipline. WK4 Engineering Specialist Knowledge Engineering specialist knowledge providing theoretical frameworks and bodies of knowledge for accepted practice areas; including knowledge at the forefront of the discipline. WK5 Engineering Design & Operations Knowledge supporting engineering design and operations, including efficient resource use, environmental impacts, whole-life cost, reuse of resources, net-zero carbon and related concepts. WK6 Engineering Practice & Technology Knowledge of engineering practice and technology in the practice areas of the engineering discipline. WK7 Engineering, Society & Sustainability Knowledge of the role of engineering in society and identified issues in engineering practice, including professional responsibility, public safety and sustainable development. WK8 Research, Critical Thinking & Creativity Engagement with current research literature, critical thinking and creative approaches for evaluating emerging issues in the discipline. title: Overview
content: Society Number : 16 of 2009 St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology is all set to have an Alumni association. SACET ALUMNI MOTTO “To go forth with values that we have learned at SACET and share them with family and the community at large”. “Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.” St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology will offer a wide range of resources for alumni, including Refresher Courses, Post Graduate Information, Higher Educational Opportunities in India or Abroad. Some of the main objectives of the alumni association will be :- To enhance the interaction between the past and present students. To enhance and modernize the existing facilities of the college. To provide industrial training, placements and other facilities to the students with the assistance of the past students. To circulate books to the students who are in need. To promote cultural, sports and other extracurricular activities. To Provide monetary assistance to the deserving students Alumni are the strength of the St. Ann’s College of Engineering & Technology. SACET takes great pride in the Alumni as the members are all in highly respectable professional positions in various industries and are closely associated with the college. Every Year College organizes an Alumni meeting to provide a platform for the seniors to give suggestions and experiences to the juniors on career, industry opportunities, higher education (India / Overseas), Feedback / Suggestions for improvement on training etc.
